title: One operation lemma per component: ilock_cycle preserves ilock_type_inv
intent: The cyclic interlocking controller ilock_cycle is a sequential composition of four operations (set_relays ;; clear_relays ;; set_switches ;; set_signals). The type-invariant theorem gives each operation its own Hoare-triple preservation lemma {ilock_type_inv} op {ilock_type_inv}, proved by one shared method, so the main theorem is just unfold ilock_cycle_def, hoare_split, and one rule application per component.

parent.name: ilock_cycle
parent.note: The parent is an anonymous lemma: the source writes `lemma "…"` with no identifier, so `ilock_cycle` here names the program whose invariant is proved, not a lemma name.

applicability.goal_shape: A Hoare triple {ilock_type_inv} P {ilock_type_inv} whose program P is a fixed sequential composition of operations (set_relays ;; clear_relays ;; set_switches ;; set_signals) and whose invariant is a conjunction of vector-size equalities (#(cdv)=11, #(tc)=4, #(relays)=5, #(signals)=3, #(switches)=5).
applicability.use_when: the program is a named sequential composition of operations and the same invariant must hold across each of them; give each operation a preservation lemma and let the main theorem be `unfold <def>`, `hoare_split`, then one `rule` per component, so each operation's lemma is a bounded, independently checkable unit.
applicability.avoid_when: an operation's preservation genuinely needs a stronger precondition than the shared invariant alone (the file's switches/signals sections fall back to a different tactic for exactly that reason); or the operations share a substantial common sub-proof that should be one shared lemma rather than repeated per component.

claims.claim: set_relays_type_inv occurs in the parent site (lines 193-200).
Lines 173-200 of fmi/Interlocking.thy contain no sorry.

The shape is a measurement: an 8-line parent (193-200) whose proof body is four `rule` applications plus `done` delegates the invariant proof to four children of 4 lines each — set_relays_type_inv 173-176, clear_relays_type_inv 178-181, set_switches_type_inv 183-186, set_signals_type_inv 188-191 — for direct_lemmas 4, glue_lines 8, child_lines [4,4,4,4].
claims.evidence: line counts at the pinned commit: 200-193+1 = 8; each child 176-173+1 = 4, in https://github.com/isabelle-utp/utp-main/blob/ffd472022798e60f0385030682b7a07fbeb49e68/fmi/Interlocking.thy

claims.claim: The authors state the decomposition in a comment at line 89: "We break down the cyclic behaviour into four separate operations."

The same per-component decomposition is reused verbatim for the relays invariant: the anonymous lemma at 308-315 unfolds ilock_cycle_def, hoare_splits, and applies set_relays_relays_inv, clear_relays_relays_inv, set_switches_relays_inv, set_signals_relays_inv (292-306), each closed by ilock_relays_inv_tac.

metrics.how_counted: parent = 193-200 (8 lines); children = 173-176, 178-181, 183-186, 188-191 (4 lines each); depth chain: children -> ilock_type_inv_rules (154-161) -> inv_subst_weakening_lemma (17-20)

consequences: The move creates one named obligation per operation, all with the same precondition/invariant {ilock_type_inv} op {ilock_type_inv}, so each closes by the same method ilock_type_inv_tac after unfolding its operation's definition. The parent's hoare_split turns the sequential composition into one goal per component, and the proof closes only if every component has a lemma; a missing component leaves an unproved goal, not a silent gap. The four children are independent (none cites a sibling) but all depend on the shared lemma ilock_type_inv_rules (depth 2) and its own dependency inv_subst_weakening_lemma (depth 3), so a defect there breaks all four at once. Adding a fifth operation to the composition requires one more child lemma and one more `rule` line. The uniform method only works because each operation preserves the type invariant outright; the file's later switches/signals sections need a stronger precondition, so their preservation lemmas fall back to a heavier tactic.
